course_name_original: Diseño de Sistemas Electrónicos de Potencia
prerequisites: General knowledge of English in oral expression, equivalent to B2 level

learning_outcomes.text: Select semiconductor devices and power capacitors for a known application.
Calculate power magnetic components (coils and transformers) for a known application.
Understand the operation of controlled and semi-controlled single-phase and three-phase rectifiers and calculate the voltages and currents in their components.
Understand the operation of single-phase AC/AC converters without frequency change and calculate the voltages and currents in their components.
Perform a complete design of the power stage of a DC/DC converter and its control circuit, as well as obtain a small-signal model of it to close its control loop.

Understand the problems caused to the electrical distribution network by the injection of low-frequency current harmonics generated by electronic (non-linear) loads, apply the regulations that limit said injection, and propose solutions.
Analyze the operation of some simple power electronic systems.

syllabus_topics: Control circuits: Types of control circuits. Constant frequency and variable duty cycle circuits. Analysis of a constant frequency control circuit example. Variable frequency and constant conduction time circuits.

Selection of power electronic devices: Curves for selecting power diodes. Static curves for selecting power MOSFET transistors. Study of power MOSFET transistor switching. Static and dynamic curves for selecting insulated gate bipolar transistors (IGBTs). The Silicon Controlled Rectifier (SCR). The Gate Turn-Off thyristor (GTO). The Triode for Alternating Current (TRIAC).
Design of magnetic components for power electronic converters: General equations. Coil design. Transformer design. Magnetic integration.

General considerations on DC/DC conversion: Comparison of conversion with linear and switched converters. Importance of conversion efficiency and its technical and environmental consequences. Environmental importance of energy saving.

Design of non-galvanically isolated DC/DC converters in steady state: Conduction mode of a DC/DC converter. Buck converter design. Boost converter design. Buck-boost converter design. The SEPIC converter. The Cuk converter.

Design of galvanically isolated DC/DC converters in steady state: Incorporation of galvanic isolation with a transformer and its importance for user safety. Forward converter design. The Cuk converter with transformer. Incorporation of galvanic isolation with multi-winding coils. Flyback converter design. The SEPIC converter with galvanic isolation.

Design of DC/DC converters with several transistors in steady state: The forward converter with active clamping. Half-bridge converter design. Push-pull converter design. Full-bridge converter design. Bidirectional converters. Importance of bidirectional converters for electrical energy storage in batteries, in the context of energy sources with low environmental impact. Bidirectional converters for energy saving in regenerative braking in transport.

Design of DC/DC converters in dynamic regime: Dynamic modeling of DC/DC converters in continuous conduction mode. Dynamic modeling of DC/DC converters in discontinuous conduction mode. Design of regulators for DC/DC converters.

Single-phase AC/DC converters with low harmonic injection into the grid: Importance of low low-frequency harmonic contamination in the electrical distribution network: IEC-61000-3-2 Standard. Concept of resistance emulator. Resistance emulators controlled by analog multiplier. Other resistance emulators.
Controlled rectifiers: Half-wave controlled rectifiers. Full-wave controlled rectifiers. Controlled rectifiers used as non-self-commutated inverters. Semi-controlled rectifiers.
AC-AC conversion without frequency change: The phase controller. Applications of the phase controller in energy saving in domestic applications.

Examples of power electronic system architectures: Power supply systems for telecommunications equipment. Converters for collector motor control. Converters for induction motors. Converters for powering high energy efficiency lighting equipment.
Brief introduction to basic elements of oral presentations: structure, discourse markers, vocal techniques, referential language applied to visual aids, etc.

assessment_methods.method: Work (T) - oral presentation in English of a work on the operation and calculation of a DC/DC converter
Laboratory Practices (PL) - results obtained from the DC/DC converter designed and built

assessment_rules: For the ordinary call, the theoretical block grade is calculated as (0.6 * EF1) + (0.2 * T), and the practical block grade as (0.2 * PL). The final grade is Theory + Practicals. For the extraordinary call, the final grade is (0.6 * EF2) + (0.2 * T) + (0.2 * PL). Grades obtained for the Work (T) and Laboratory Practices (PL) are carried over only within the same academic year. For differentiated evaluation, the final grade is (0.8 * EF) + (0.2 * T).
